lyrics:
[Intro: bright piano figure, soft kick, street sounds]

[Verse 1: conversational male rap]
I was fifteen when I heard a dead man say it wouldn't shift
Thirty years I've walked this block, so let me tell you how I lived
Corner store's a pharmacy, the pharmacy's a bank
The bank became a coffee place, so I don't know who to thank
My son's got friends in every shade, they don't think twice
That's real. I didn't have that. That's nice.
But he still gets the talk before he drives at night
Same words my mother used. Hands in sight.

[Chorus: sung, male tenor with a small choir]
Some of it moved
And some of it stayed
Some of it's better than the day I was made
I'm not gonna lie to you either way
Some of it moved, and some of it stayed

[Verse 2: rap, a little more heat]
They closed the rec, then built it back with glass
The rent went up so fast my neighbors couldn't last
We got a mayor looks like us, and potholes just the same
I learned that faces change before the game
But I've seen a kid from here go be a judge
I've seen the old heads teaching, holding no grudge
I've seen a funeral turn into a vote
I keep the wins. I write 'em down. I keep the note.

[Chorus: sung, male tenor with a small choir]
Some of it moved
And some of it stayed
Some of it's better than the day I was made
I'm not gonna lie to you either way
Some of it moved, and some of it stayed

[Verse 3: quieter, to his son]
So, son, don't let 'em tell you nothing gives
And don't let 'em tell you it's all fixed
Both of those are easy. Both are lies.
You push the part in front of you. That's how it's sized.

[Final Chorus: full choir, piano brighter]
Some of it moved
And some of it stayed
Some of it's better than the day I was made
I'm not gonna lie to you either way
Some of it moved, 'cause somebody pushed

[Outro: piano figure, a basketball bouncing, fading]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 88 BPM, 4/4, G minor with a hopeful lift in the chorus. Mid-slow, steady and warm.

VOICE: Male, mid-range, relaxed and conversational, rapped as if talking across a kitchen table, with some heat in verse 2 and tenderness in verse 3. The chorus is sung by a smooth male tenor with a small mixed choir.

INSTRUMENTS: A bright, rolling acoustic piano figure, a boom-bap kick and snare, a round bass guitar, soft strings, a gospel choir, a little wah guitar, street and playground sounds.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:56 Chorus 1. 1:20 Verse 2. 2:04 Chorus 2. 2:28 Verse 3, quieter. 2:52 Final chorus, last line changed. 3:20 Outro, piano and a basketball, ends 3:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1990s West Coast conscious rap: warm, clear and piano-led, drums soft, vocal natural.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The last chorus ending ''cause somebody pushed' at 3:14.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original, from the 1990s, doubts anything will change. A man who has lived the thirty years since can report exactly what did and did not, and tell his son both halves.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Weary, fair, stirred, instructing.
